items.title: Type and Extent of Control
items.intent: Outsourced and external work does not weaken the organization's ability to deliver conforming product. Controls on the provider and on its output are set according to impact and risk, and verification is proportionate, including inspection or testing where counterfeit or high risk exists.
items.question: For one external provider, show the controls you set on the provider and on its output, and the verification you chose based on risk.
evidence: Control definition for the provider and its output
Risk basis for the verification extent
failure_modes: Provider output released without verification or traceability for pending verification

items.title: Information for External Providers
items.intent: Requirements given to providers are adequate before they are sent, and cover processes, approvals, competence, performance control, verification, special characteristics, counterfeit prevention, change notification, flow-down, access rights and awareness.
items.question: Show the purchasing information you sent to one provider for a critical item, and how it covers approval, change notification and flow-down.
evidence: Purchase order or purchasing information package
Flow-down of applicable customer and regulatory requirements
Access rights clause for the organization, customers and regulators
failure_modes: Purchasing information omits flow-down of customer or regulatory requirements
No right of access for customer or regulator

items.title: Production and Service Provision
items.intent: Production and service are carried out under controlled conditions.
items.question: Show me how production or service is run under controlled conditions for one job.

items.title: Control of Production and Service Provision
items.intent: Production has defined characteristics and results, suitable measurement, criteria for acceptance, competent people, validation of processes that cannot be verified later, prevention of human error, release and delivery controls, workmanship criteria, traceability of products during production, control of critical items, in-process inspection points, foreign object control, utilities, and records that operations were completed as planned.
items.question: Pick one job and show: the defined characteristics, acceptance criteria, in-process inspection points, critical-item controls, and the record that every operation was completed.
evidence: Traveler or work order with characteristics and acceptance criteria
Critical item or key characteristic records

items.title: Control of Equipment, Tools, and Software Programs
items.intent: Equipment, tools and software used for production or measurement are validated before production release and maintained. Stored production tooling has defined storage requirements and condition checks.
items.question: Show the validation of one piece of production software or tooling, and the storage and condition checks for stored tooling.
evidence: Storage requirement and condition check records

items.title: Validation and Control of Special Processes
items.intent: Special processes whose output cannot be fully verified later are approved, their conditions maintained, facilities and people qualified, methods defined, and records kept.
items.question: Show the approval and qualification arrangements for one special process, such as welding or heat treatment, and the records that prove it is kept within conditions.
evidence: Qualification of facilities, equipment and people
failure_modes: Special process run without approval or qualified people

items.title: Production Process Verification
items.intent: Production processes are verified to produce conforming product, a representative first-run item is verified, and this is repeated when changes invalidate earlier results.
items.question: Show the first article verification for a new part, and the trigger that required it to be repeated after a process change.
failure_modes: First article not performed for a new part
No repeat after a change that invalidated results

items.title: Identification and Traceability
items.intent: Outputs are identified, their configuration is known, their status against inspection is shown, acceptance authority media are controlled, and traceability is maintained where required.
items.question: Pick a product in production: show its identification, configuration, inspection status, and how it could be traced back through its materials and steps.
evidence: Identification on the product or its travelers
Traceability record from material batch through to delivery

items.title: Property Belonging to Customers or External Providers
items.intent: Customer or provider property is cared for, identified, verified, protected, and any loss or damage is reported.
items.question: Show how customer-owned property on site is identified and protected, and what happened when some was found damaged.
evidence: Report to the customer on loss or damage

items.title: Preservation
items.intent: Outputs are preserved during production and service, covering identification, handling, contamination control, packaging, storage, transport and protection, including cleaning, foreign object control, marking, shelf life and hazardous materials as they apply.
items.question: Show how a finished item is preserved from the bench to the shipment, including any shelf-life or hazardous material controls.

items.title: Post-Delivery Activities
items.intent: Post-delivery obligations are met and their extent is set by regulatory needs, consequences, customer requirements and feedback. Problems found after delivery are investigated and reported.
items.question: Show a problem reported after delivery: how it was investigated and reported.
evidence: Technical documentation control for maintenance or repair

items.title: Control of Changes
items.intent: Production and service changes are reviewed and controlled, persons authorized to approve them are named, and the review results are kept.
items.question: Show the last production change, its review, and the named person who authorized it.
evidence: List of persons authorized to approve changes
failure_modes: Changes made without review or named authority

items.title: Release of Products and Services
items.intent: Products are not released until the planned verification is satisfactorily completed. Release records show conformity to acceptance criteria and who authorized release, and all required documents travel with the product.
items.question: Show a release record for one product: the acceptance evidence and who authorized release.
evidence: Release record with acceptance evidence and named authorizer
Documents accompanying the product at delivery

items.title: Control of Nonconforming Outputs
items.intent: Nonconforming outputs are identified, controlled and prevented from unintended use or delivery. Disposition is by an authorized person, use-as-is or repair is approved by the design authority and the customer where the contract is departed from, scrap is marked, and counterfeit parts are kept out of the supply chain.
items.question: Show one nonconforming item: how it was identified, contained, dispositioned and by whom.
evidence: Disposition approval by the authorized person
Design authority or customer approval where required
failure_modes: Use-as-is approved without design authority or customer approval

items.title: Nonconforming outputs control process
items.intent: The nonconformity control process defines responsibility and approval of disposition, containment, timely reporting to customers, and corrective action for nonconformities found after delivery.
items.question: Show the nonconformity control process: who decides disposition, how containment is done, and how customers are told.
evidence: Customer notification record for a delivered nonconformity
failure_modes: Customers not notified of delivered nonconformities

items.title: Retained nonconformity information
items.intent: Records describe the nonconformity, the actions taken, any concessions, and the authority that decided.
items.question: Show the record for one nonconformity with its actions, any concession and the deciding authority.
evidence: Nonconformity record with description, actions, concession and authority

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis, and Evaluation
items.intent: The organization decides what to monitor and measure, how, when, and when to analyse and evaluate, and evaluates QMS performance and effectiveness.
items.question: Show what you monitor, how it is analysed, and how it has changed what you do.

items.title: General
items.intent: Monitoring methods give valid results and the QMS performance and effectiveness are evaluated and recorded.
items.question: Show the QMS performance evaluation for the last period.

items.title: Customer Satisfaction
items.intent: Customer perceptions are monitored and reviewed, including conformity, on-time delivery, complaints and corrective action requests, and improvement plans address deficiencies.
items.question: How do you collect customer perception, and what did you change because of it?

items.title: Analysis and Evaluation
items.intent: Monitoring data is analysed to evaluate product conformity, customer satisfaction, QMS performance, planning, risk actions, provider performance, and improvement needs.
items.question: Show the analysis that evaluated provider performance in the last period and what it led to.
evidence: Analysis report covering the required areas
failure_modes: Analysis does not cover provider performance

items.title: Internal Audit
items.intent: Internal audits run at planned intervals and show whether the QMS conforms to the organization's and the standard's requirements and is effectively implemented.
items.question: Show your internal audit programme and the last audit's findings and follow-up.
evidence: Audit programme with frequency and scope

items.title: Internal audit scope
items.intent: Audits check conformity to the organization's requirements and the standard, and whether the QMS is effectively implemented and maintained.
items.question: For your last internal audit, show the criteria it checked against and the conclusion on effective implementation.

items.title: Audit programme and conduct
items.intent: An audit programme exists with frequency, method, responsibilities, planning and reporting, considering process importance, change and previous results. Each audit has criteria and scope, auditors are selected for objectivity and impartiality, results go to management, corrections are made promptly, and records are kept.
items.question: Show the audit programme, how the auditors were selected for impartiality, and how results were reported to management.

items.title: Management Review
items.intent: Top management reviews the QMS at planned intervals for suitability, adequacy, effectiveness and alignment with strategy.
items.question: Show the most recent management review: its date, attendees and what it reviewed.

items.title: General
items.intent: Management reviews the QMS at planned intervals for continuing suitability, adequacy, effectiveness and strategic alignment.
items.question: What is your planned interval for management review and when did the last one happen?
failure_modes: Review not held at planned intervals

items.title: Management Review Inputs
items.intent: The review considers action status from earlier reviews, changes in context, QMS performance trends (customer, objectives, process, nonconformities and corrective actions, measurement, audit results, providers, on-time delivery), resource adequacy, risk action effectiveness, and improvement opportunities.
items.question: Show the inputs to the last management review and confirm each required area was covered.
evidence: Management review input pack covering each required area

items.title: Management Review Outputs
items.intent: Outputs include decisions and actions on improvement, QMS changes, resource needs and risks, and results are kept.
items.question: Show the actions and decisions from the last review and their owners.
evidence: Review outputs with actions and owners

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: General
items.intent: Improvement opportunities are selected and actions taken to meet customer requirements and enhance satisfaction, covering product improvement, correction and prevention, and QMS performance.
items.question: Show two improvement actions from the last year and how they were selected.
evidence: Improvement action records with selection basis

items.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
items.intent: Corrective action is managed: nonconformities are controlled and corrected, causes are found and removed, similar nonconformities are checked, effectiveness is reviewed, and the process is documented.
items.question: Pick one nonconformity: show the containment, the root cause, the corrective action and the evidence it worked.
evidence: Corrective action record with root cause

items.title: Corrective action process
items.intent: When a nonconformity occurs the organization reacts, controls and corrects it, deals with consequences, evaluates the need for action to stop recurrence, implements action, reviews effectiveness, updates risks, changes the QMS if needed, flows requirements to providers when they are responsible, and escalates when action is not timely or effective.
items.question: Show the corrective action for one nonconformity, from reaction through to the effectiveness review, and what you did when it was late.
evidence: Corrective action record through all steps
Flow-down to a provider where responsible
Escalation record for a late action
failure_modes: Corrective action closed without effectiveness review
No escalation when action was late

items.title: Corrective action records
items.intent: Records show the nature of nonconformities, actions taken, and the results of corrective action.
items.question: Show the records for one corrective action: the nonconformity, the actions and the result.

items.title: Continual Improvement
items.intent: The QMS suitability, adequacy and effectiveness are continually improved, using analysis, evaluation and management review outputs, and improvement activities are monitored for effect.
items.question: Show an improvement that followed from the management review, and how you checked it worked.
